To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transit route choice model calibrated with the revealed preference data from smartcard transactions can provide a more realistic and accurate result than the model calibrated with the stated preference data from the survey.

a multinomial logit model with six explanatory variables can be calibrated with the revealed preference data of smartcard transaction records in a multimodal urban transit network, and the calibrated model shows good performance in predicting route choice of transit passengers.
the transit route choice model calibrated by the population data of revealed preferences from smartcard transaction record can provide more realistic and reliable results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.

the development of an advanced transit route choice model that can be used for the transit planning and operation in the Seoul metropolitan area, which is one of the largest and most congested multimodal transit systems in the world.

the calibration of a route choice model using the revealed preference data of the transit smartcard in a large scale multimodal transit network, and it is the first attempt to analyze the route choices of transit passengers using the revealed preference of smartcard data in a complex transit network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calibrated model can be used for transit planning purposes such as transit network design and transit fare policy.

it is possible to build a transit network that is abstract but still has enough information to represent a complex transit system, and that it is possible and useful to calibrate a transit route choice models using revealed preference data of smartcard.
the calibration result of this study is statistically and logically good to include six explanatory variables in utility function of the MNL model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model is able to estimate the route choice behavior in the complex multimodal transit system and to provide more realistic results.

this study has developed a method to build an abstract transit network from a huge scale transit data of smartcard transaction records, and it has successfully applied this method in a complex and huge scale multimodal transit network of a big city.
this study successfully developed a transit route choice modeling framework that could be applied to the real transit network with a large scale of OD pairs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smartcard data can be used to estimate route choice behavior of the transit passengers in a complex transit system.

we have shown that a revealed preference model of transit route choice behavior can be built with a large amount of population data from the smartcard transaction records in a multimodal and complex transit network.
the calibration result showed that the model is statistically significant to include the six variables in the utility model, which is the main contribution of this study.
